parole.testo: From Germanic, from Frankish *bîsi (“covered with clouds”), related to *bisa (“wind from the northeast”), from Proto-Germanic *bī̆s- (“to storm ahead”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰeyh₂- (“to be afraid, fear”), see also Proto-Germanic *bibāną (“to shiver”). Compare Walloon bijhe.
Inherited from Old French bordure, bordeüre, from border (“to border”), from bort, bord (“a border”), of Germanic origin, from Frankish *bord.

Inherited from Middle French crosse, from Old French crosse (“shepherd's staff”), from a Germanic language, likely Frankish *krukkju, ultimately from Proto-Germanic *krukjō (“staff, crutch”). Compare Old High German krucka, Old Saxon krukka, Middle Dutch crucke, English crutch.

From a modification, based on guide, of Old French guier (compare also Old Occitan guidar, guida), of Germanic origin; e.g. Frankish *wītan, Proto-Germanic *wītaną, possibly through an Early Medieval Latin intermediary. Compare Italian guidare, Spanish guiar.
From harer (“to set a dog on”), of Germanic origin, from Frankish *hara (“here, hither”), from Proto-Germanic *hē₂r (“here, hither”).
Inherited from Middle French and Old French heron, of Germanic origin, from Old Frankish *herigo, *hraigrō, from Proto-Germanic *haigrô, *hraigrô. Compare Old High German heigaro.

Inherited from Middle French latte, from Old French latte, late, from a Germanic source, probably Frankish *lattu. See also German Latte, Dutch lat, and English lath and lattice.

Inherited from Middle French nique, from Old French nic, of Germanic origin, from Frankish *hnukēn, ultimately from Proto-Germanic *hnukāną (“to be bent, wrinkle”), similar to Swedish nyck (“whim, fancy”).

Inherited from Middle French riper, ripper, from Old French riper, of Germanic origin, ultimately from Frankish *wrīban (“to rub”). Compare Dutch wrijven, German reiben.

parole.significato: tuft, clump, bunch of feathers, grass or hair, etc., held together at the base
parole.testo: Of Germanic origin, from Frankish *topp (“tuft”). Akin to toupet and modern German Zopf.
